name: Tempester n°64: the Voice OS version of each chip, reported after the exact version (request 43 -> the 43 reply, then F0 01 28 45 <6 x 3 bytes> F7)
explanation: Dependencies: n°1 (patch/dump_request.json, byte sender 0x9d07a080) and n°39 in its 1.6.7.0 copy patch/version_request_1670.json, which leaves this patch the word 0x9d07b45c. Why: the identity reply carries the Voice version only on a DSI Main (n°1 sends the constant 0x7F2), so nothing outside the machine could tell which Voice OS each chip runs (0x15 DSI 1.5, 0x16 Tempester Voice 1.5.1.0). After n°39's 43 reply, byte for byte as before (its F7 is still sent first), the machine sends F0 01 28 45 then, for chips 0-5, the reply word v main read once at start-up (0xFE00, [address], what System > Voice OS Version shows) as v >> 14, (v >> 7) & 0x7F, v & 0x7F, then F7 (23 bytes), on the cable set in System. All 16 bits are sent: a chip that did not answer is seen as such. 45 is no command of the machine. Hook 0x9d07b45c (n°39's last jal); code 0x9d07b600-0x9d07b68f; no RAM. Proof: tools/sim_version_request.py --voice-versions and its counter-proofs. Source: voice_versions.s.

edits.why: jal 0x9d07b600 ; n°39, the 43 reply's F7: was "jal 0x9d07a080" (sent first by VOICE_VERSIONS). Delay slot "li a0,0xf7" kept
addiu sp,sp,-0x20 ; called by n°39 with a0 = 0xF7, the end of the 43 reply
jal 0x9d07a080 ; n°1's sender: byte a0 on the cable set in System ([address])
